equivalent_formulations.reasoning: f(n,m) as used by Kominers equals the least interval length for a given start, and F(n)=max_m f(n,m). Chen uses the same F(n); the original Erdős–Pomerance f(n) is a diagonal *endpoint*, not our uniform length. The Hall bipartite matching criterion is equivalent to the distinct-multiple problem, but not itself an exact finite value.

value.rationale: F(n) is the classical natural uniform-length invariant in an active 2026 problem. n=17 is proved to be the earliest strict excess over the elementary optimal candidate 2n-2, not a selected arbitrary slice; 32 exceptional period classes and an explicit Hall witness explain the first boundary. A natural complete small-parameter threshold is useful for future searches and structural methods. Does not claim broad asymptotic novelty.
